title: Build anyway (Nehemiah 4:11)
hookLine: the wall is rebuilt with a tool in one hand and a weapon in the other
carry: one hand on the stone, one hand ready
last: THE SLOW WORK WAS DONE BEFORE.

lines: THE WALL GOES UP ON ITS OLD LINES.
cards: First come the jokes. Nehemiah has rallied the people, and they're raising the wall of Jerusalem on its old lines, family by family, each beside its own stretch.

Across the way, the local strongmen Sanballat and Tobiah laugh. In the King James words, Sanballat sneers, "What do these feeble Jews?" Tobiah adds that if a fox went up on it, it would break their stone wall down.
The jokes don't stop the work, so they turn into threats: a plan to come and fight against Jerusalem. Now the builders have a choice. Stop until it's safe, or find a way to keep going.

teach.b: Nehemiah does two things at once, side by side: "Nevertheless we made our prayer unto our God, and set a watch against them day and night." Prayer and a guard, together. Then he reorganizes the site.
Half the young men work, half stand ready, with the people's leaders behind every section. And here is the picture this day is named for.

teach.h: ONE HAND WORKS, ONE HAND GUARDS.
teach.b: The verse is numbered eleven in Hebrew Bibles and seventeen in the King James: "every one with one of his hands wrought in the work, and with the other hand held a weapon."
The builders wear swords at their sides while they lay brick.

A man with a shofar, a ram's horn, stands next to Nehemiah, and the plan is simple: wherever you hear the horn, gather to us there; our God will fight for us. They work from first light until the stars come out.
Nehemiah and his men don't even take off their clothes, except for washing. They don't wait for the threats to go away, and they don't pretend the threats aren't real. They hold both.

teach.h: THE PEOPLE HAD A MIND TO WORK.
teach.b: Earlier, the text gives the reason the wall kept rising at all: the people had a mind to work.
A hard week, a project people laugh at, a goal someone wants to stop: the wall in Nehemiah was built by people with only one hand free.

how: Some Jewish readers turn to Nehemiah's builders, working with one hand and guarding with the other, as a picture of carrying on with a community's work under threat.

o: drop the work and fight the people who mock you
keep working on what matters while staying on guard
wait until every threat is gone, then start

games.q: the building of the wall — tap the pairs.
p: a fox would break it down
one hand works, one holds a weapon

s: Nehemiah stopped the work until the threats passed
they kept building, with half the men working and half standing guard.
the text puts prayer and a guard side by side
"we made our prayer unto our God, and set a watch against them day and night."
the verse is numbered the same in every Bible
it's 4:11 in Hebrew Bibles and 4:17 in the King James.

games.q: you're Nehemiah. the wall is half built, and enemies are planning an attack. what do you do?
o: keep building, armed and on watch.
ignore the threats and carry on as before.
games.why: they pray, set a watch, and build with one hand while the other holds a weapon. they neither stop nor pretend the danger isn't there.

practice: Rest your hands on your knees, palms up.

Let one hand hold something you're building, a family, a habit, a piece of work, and the other whatever pushes against it, doubt, tiredness, a real worry, and ask what one brick you could still lay with both in hand.
If you pray, bring both hands to God, the way Nehemiah's builders prayed and kept watch.

wordCard.voice: Build anyway. The wall of Jerusalem goes up with a tool in one hand and a weapon in the other, because the people had a mind to work. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: wall, the word for what Nehemiah's people are rebuilding.

carryVoice: Your line: one hand on the stone, one hand ready. The threats were real, and the wall went up anyway. That's day eight hundred seventy-eight.
